$help: Audit of the English V-SIL v3 paper (methodology/V-SIL-v3/V-SIL_v3.md). Format: tools/README.md.

context.title: V-SIL v3: Adaptive Stage-Gate Lifecycle for COTS-Constrained Verified Prototype Development
context.domain: Software engineering methodology: verification and validation of software on COTS hardware (SDR / embedded), AI-agent-assisted development
context.problem: AI coding agents can produce software quickly, but their claims of correctness are hard to trust: the model may approve its own work, evidence rarely states the environment it was produced in (logic, simulation or real hardware), and when requirements cannot be met on the chosen COTS hardware there is no formal way to send that back to the requirements author instead of silently weakening the implementation.
context.idea: A stage-gate lifecycle that takes a finalised Build Package (PRD with measurable constraints, COTS hardware envelope, acceptance criteria) and delivers either a Verified Prototype with per-module evidence or a formal Request for Deviation (RFD). Stages and gates: S0 normalises the Build Package into IEEE 29148 StRS/SyRS blueprints; G0 is a deterministic, script-only structural validation followed by a human Gate H; S1 designs a layered architecture (base layer + plug-in modules) with a component dependency DAG, typed interface contracts and per-module verification profiles; G1 validates DAG acyclicity, contract completeness, SYS-* coverage, stub feasibility and profile consistency; S2 implements base layer first, then each module in DAG order, with sandwich (top-down with stubs + bottom-up with drivers) integration; G2 is an adaptive verification gate with levels VL-0 (logic, mandatory), VL-1 (Mock/SIL, optional) and VL-2 (HIL, optional), chosen per module per cycle under a floor rule and an honesty rule. Failures are routed either internally as defects (to S1 or S2) or externally as an RFD with evidence, trade-off options and impact analysis.
context.constraints: Develops, tests and validates software only; it does not design hardware. All hardware is commercial off-the-shelf and is treated as a fixed envelope. Ground truth is human-authored Markdown following the IEEE/ISO/IEC 29148:2018 document family. The method must be agent-agnostic (usable with any AI coding agent). G0 must be deterministic and use no AI. Governing principles P1-P4: HITL is an authorisation barrier and HIL a validation barrier; oracle differs from generator; mechanical rejection beats LLM approval; verified differs from validated.
context.assumptions: The Build Package is finalised before S0 and its constraints are measurable. S0 can normalise content without making judgements about sufficiency or scope. Interface contracts can always be specified completely enough to write deterministic stubs. Modules can communicate only through base-layer interfaces. VL-0 (unit + sandwich integration) is a sufficient floor for every module in every cycle. Gate failures can be reliably classified as either internal defects or requirement infeasibility. The terminology mapping to IEEE 29119, ISO 26262, SDAD, ECSS and MIL-HDBK-61A is accurate.
context.prior: Predecessor: V-SIL v2 (methodology/V-SIL-v2/V-SIL.tex in the same repository), a continuous V-model at the SIL tier. Related work cited by the paper: sandwich integration testing (Pressman; ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119), contract testing, layered architectures (Bass et al.), ISO 26262 verification levels, SDAD spec crystallisation, the Coordinator-Implementor-Verifier pattern, the HAL mock to SIL to HIL substitution ladder, LLM-as-a-judge limitations, and RFD / deviation processes in ECSS-Q-ST-10-09C, MIL-HDBK-61A and NASA NPR 7150.2.

dimensions.name: Technical feasibility
dimensions.definition: Can a team using AI coding agents and the stated tooling execute every stage and gate as written, on COTS hardware, without unstated steps?
dimensions.low: Key stages or gates cannot be executed as described, or depend on capabilities that do not exist.
dimensions.mid: Executable, but some stages or gates need unstated procedures, tools or decisions.
dimensions.high: Every stage and gate has defined inputs, outputs, criteria and an executor; nothing essential is left implicit.

dimensions.name: Novelty
dimensions.definition: How does V-SIL v3 differ from existing lifecycles (V-model, stage-gate, ISO 26262 / 29119 practice, SDAD, spec-driven development, V-SIL v2)? Judge only after the prior-art check.
dimensions.low: A renaming or repackaging of existing practice.
dimensions.mid: Known elements combined with a meaningful twist (e.g. adaptive per-module VL, defect vs RFD routing).
dimensions.high: A clear, verified difference with a defensible advantage over the named prior work.

dimensions.name: Impact
dimensions.definition: How much does the method improve the trustworthiness and delivery of agent-built software on COTS hardware, and for whom?
dimensions.low: Marginal benefit over ordinary test-driven development.
dimensions.mid: Clear benefit for a defined group (e.g. SDR / embedded research labs).
dimensions.high: Large, measurable benefit addressing a critical gap in AI-assisted verified development.

dimensions.name: Groundedness
dimensions.definition: Are the claims, terminology mappings and principles traceable to the cited sources, and are the cited sources appropriate and verifiable?
dimensions.low: Claims and mappings are unsupported or cite unsuitable sources.
dimensions.mid: Most mappings sourced; some claims or sources weak, informal or unverifiable.
dimensions.high: Every mapping and principle traced to a specific, appropriate, verifiable source.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.definition: Is the methodology specified precisely enough that two independent teams would apply it the same way?
dimensions.low: Vague; stages, gates or routing could be read in conflicting ways.
dimensions.mid: Mostly specified; some criteria, roles or artefacts undefined.
dimensions.high: Precise and testable: every gate has explicit pass/fail criteria, every route a trigger, every artefact a format.

checks: Structural: the paper has an abstract, terminology, a section for every stage and gate (S0, G0, S1, G1, S2, G2), feedback routing, terminal output and references, in a logical order.
Internal consistency: numbers, labels and levels in the text match the tables, code blocks and Mermaid diagrams; claims do not contradict each other.

Diagram-text agreement: every transition drawn in a Mermaid diagram (PASS, FAIL, design, module, infeasible, updated) is described in the prose, and every route described in the prose appears in a diagram.
Gate completeness: every gate states its question, its pass/fail criteria, who or what decides (script, human, agent), and where each outcome routes.
Terminology: every term and acronym (Build Package, GT, HITL, HIL, SIL, VL-0/1/2, DAG, RFD, Gate H, sandwich integration) is defined once and used uniformly, including in the Terminology table.
Standards mapping: each row of the Terminology table maps to a term that the cited source actually uses with that meaning.
Principles applied: each governing principle P1-P4 is reflected in at least one concrete rule of a stage or gate, and no rule contradicts one.

Verification levels: the definitions of VL-0, VL-1 and VL-2, the floor and honesty rules, the G2 sub-gates, the scenario table and the honesty declaration in the terminal output are mutually consistent.

Worked examples: the SDR FM dependency graph, the verification-profile table, the RFD-001 example and the terminal output agree with each other and obey the stated rules (e.g. hw_dependency implies required_vl VL-2).
Defect vs RFD: the criteria for classifying a gate failure as an internal defect or as infeasibility are stated and applicable, and the list of stages that can emit an RFD agrees with the diagrams.
References: every in-text citation [n] exists in the reference list, every listed reference is cited in the text, and each entry is complete enough to locate the source.
Abstract fidelity: every claim in the abstract is supported by the body, and the body introduces no core concept missing from the abstract.

[V-SIL v3 paper, English — methodology/V-SIL-v3/V-SIL_v3.md, version 3.0-draft] # V-SIL v3: Adaptive Stage-Gate Lifecycle for COTS-Constrained Verified Prototype Development **David Ramírez-Betancourt** — Universidad Nacional de Colombia, GCPDS **Version:** 3.0-draft **Date:** October 2026 --- ## Abstract V-SIL v3 is a software development methodology that receives a finalised Build Package (PRD with measurable constraints, COTS hardware envelope, and acceptance criteria) and delivers a Verified Prototype with per-module evidence — or, when the requirements are infeasible on the declared COTS platform, a formal Request for Deviation (RFD) with trade-off analysis. The methodology is built on three principles: (1) implementation proceeds module by module within a layered architecture; (2) verification depth is adaptive per module — a mandatory floor of unit testing plus sandwich integration is always enforced, while Mock/SIL and HIL levels are reached at the project's convenience; and (3) evidence is honest — every claim names the verification level at which it was produced. Terminology is aligned with IEEE/ISO/IEC 29119, ISO 26262, SDAD [6], the Coordinator-Implementor-Verifier pattern [10], the embedded HAL mock→SIL→HIL substitution ladder [11], and the ECSS/MIL-HDBK-61A Request for Deviation process [16][17]. ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef input fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#1f2937,stroke-width:2px classDef vsil fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e classDef output fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d,stroke-width:2px classDef rfd fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-width:2px IN["Build Package
PRD · COTS envelope
acceptance criteria"]:::input VSIL["V-SIL v3
S0 → G0 → S1 → G1 → S2 → G2"]:::vsil OUT["Verified Prototype
per-module VL evidence"]:::output RFD["Request for Deviation
infeasibility evidence
+ trade-off options"]:::rfd IN --> VSIL VSIL -->|nominal| OUT VSIL -.->|infeasible| RFD RFD -.->|updated Build Package| IN ``` --- ## 1 Terminology | Informal term | Standard term | Source | |---|---|---| | Propagation test (base → modules with placeholders) | **Top-down integration test with stubs** | IEEE 29119; Pressman [1] | | Backpropagation test (module → base) | **Bottom-up integration test with drivers** | IEEE 29119; Pressman [1] | | Combined propagation + backpropagation | **Sandwich (hybrid) integration testing** | IEEE 29119 [2] | | Placeholders | **Stubs** (called by the unit under test) | Standard SE | | Test harnesses simulating callers | **Drivers** (call the unit under test) | Standard SE | | Router validation | **Interface-contract verification** | Contract testing [3]; Bass et al. [4] | | Design by layers | **Layered architecture** with **component dependency graph** (DAG) | Bass et al. [4] | | Levels N0 / N1 / N2 | **Verification levels** (VL-0, VL-1, VL-2) | Adapted from ISO 26262 [5] | | Feedback to Build Package with trade-off | **Request for Deviation (RFD)** | ECSS [16]; MIL-HDBK-61A [17]; NASA NPR 7150.2 [18] | --- ## 2 Stage-Gate Overview ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef stage fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e classDef gate fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d classDef terminal fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e,stroke-width:3px classDef input fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#1f2937,stroke-width:2px classDef rfd fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d BP["Build Package"]:::input S0["S0 — Normalisation + GT"]:::stage G0{"G0 — Structural validation"}:::gate S1["S1 — Layered architecture design"]:::stage G1{"G1 — DAG + contract validation"}:::gate S2["S2 — Module-by-module implementation"]:::stage G2{"G2 — Adaptive verification"}:::gate T["Verified Prototype
per-module VL evidence"]:::terminal RFD["RFD
Request for Deviation"]:::rfd BP --> S0 S0 --> G0 G0 -->|PASS + Gate H| S1 S1 --> G1 G1 -->|PASS| S2 S2 --> G2 G2 -->|PASS| T G0 -.->|FAIL| S0 G1 -.->|FAIL| S1 G2 -.->|design| S1 G2 -.->|module| S2 S1 -.->|infeasible| RFD G2 -.->|infeasible| RFD RFD -.->|updated| BP ``` **Governing principles.** **P1.** HITL is an authorisation barrier; HIL is a validation barrier. **P2.** Oracle ≠ generator — the model never approves its own work [7]. **P3.** Mechanical rejection beats LLM approval, never the reverse [8]. **P4.** *Verified* ≠ *validated* — claims name the environment [9]. --- ## 3 S0 — Normalisation and Ground Truth ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef input fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#1f2937 classDef process fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764 classDef output fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e BP["Build Package
Obligations · COTS
constraints · QA"]:::input FILL["Fill IEEE 29148
blueprints"]:::process StRS["G0_StRS.md
§9.4"]:::output SyRS["G0_SyRS.md
§9.5"]:::output BP --> FILL FILL --> StRS FILL --> SyRS ``` S0 **normalises only** — it casts the Build Package content into the IEEE 29148 [12] document blueprints and makes no conceptual judgement about sufficiency or scope. Following SDAD Phase 1 (spec crystallisation) [6], it populates the blueprints: - **G0_StRS.md** — Stakeholder Requirements Specification (§9.4): `NRM-*`, `HWC-*`, `STK-*` blocks. - **G0_SyRS.md** — System Requirements Specification (§9.5): `SYS-*` blocks tracing to StRS. Any iteration happens afterwards at G0, which validates the Build Package content against the deterministic gate (the blueprint) — not by a review judgement here. --- ## 4 G0 — Structural Validation ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef doc fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e classDef phase fill:#f0fdf4,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d classDef gate fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d classDef fail fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d StRS["G0_StRS.md"]:::doc SyRS["G0_SyRS.md"]:::doc SCRIPT["g0_validate.py
deterministic · stdlib-only · no AI"]:::phase P1["Headings"]:::phase P2["Metadata"]:::phase P3["Block fields"]:::phase P4["Cross-doc G0-X"]:::phase G0{"G0"}:::gate PASS["PASS → Gate H"]:::gate FAIL["FAIL → edit GT"]:::fail StRS & SyRS --> SCRIPT SCRIPT --> P1 & P2 & P3 & P4 P1 & P2 & P3 & P4 --> G0 G0 -->|exit 0| PASS G0 -->|exit 1| FAIL FAIL -.->|validate vs original Build Package| S0_ S0_["S0"]:::doc ``` Deterministic. No AI. Binary verdict. After G0 passes, human Gate H asks: *Requirements complete, bounded, and verifiable?* --- ## 5 S1 — Layered Architecture Design ### 5.1 Layered architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef base fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a classDef mod fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4f46e5,color:#312e81 classDef integ fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a subgraph ARCH["S1 produces"] direction TD BASE["Base Layer
Orchestration · HAL · data routing
interface contracts"]:::base subgraph MODS["Modules"] direction LR M1["M1"]:::mod M2["M2"]:::mod M3["M3"]:::mod MN["MN"]:::mod end INT["Integration
Modules wired through base-layer interfaces"]:::integ end BASE --> MODS --> INT ``` Modules are plug-in units communicating only through the base layer's declared interfaces. No direct module-to-module calls. ### 5.2 Component dependency graph (SDR FM example) ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef hal fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d classDef dsp fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f classDef dec fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d classDef out fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e HW["HackRF"]:::hal IQ["iq_acquisition
VL-2 · HAL"]:::hal FFT["fft_engine
VL-1 · DSP"]:::dsp FE["feature_extractor
VL-1 · DSP"]:::dsp CL["classifier
VL-0 · Decision"]:::dec DEM["audio_demod
VL-1 · Output"]:::out DS["data_store
VL-0 · Output"]:::out HW -->|raw RF| IQ IQ -->|raw_iq| FFT IQ -->|raw_iq| DEM FFT -->|psd_estimate| FE FE -->|channel_features| CL CL -->|occupancy_decision| DS ``` Each edge carries an **interface contract** (data type, schema version, units, latency). The graph must be acyclic. Each node carries a **verification profile**: `module_id`, `layer`, `depends_on`, `provides`, `hw_dependency`, `required_vl`. | Module | Layer | HW dep. | Required VL | |---|---|---|---| | `iq_acquisition` | HAL | **yes** | VL-2 (HIL) | | `fft_engine` | DSP | no | VL-1 (SIL) | | `feature_extractor` | DSP | no | VL-1 (SIL) | | `classifier` | Decision | no | VL-0 (unit) | | `audio_demod` | Output | no | VL-1 (SIL) | | `data_store` | Output | no | VL-0 (unit) | --- ## 6 G1 — Dependency-Graph and Interface-Contract Validation G1 answers: *Are all implementation-critical design choices resolved?* 1. **DAG acyclicity.** No cycles. 2. **Interface completeness.** Every edge carries a typed contract. 3. **Coverage.** Every `SYS-*` traces to at least one module. 4. **Stub feasibility.** Every contract is complete enough to write a deterministic stub. 5. **Verification-profile consistency.** `hw_dependency: true` → `required_vl: VL-2`. **PASS** → S2. **FAIL** → S1. --- ## 7 S2 — Module-by-Module Implementation ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef base fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a classDef mod fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4f46e5,color:#312e81 classDef test fill:#f0fdf4,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d classDef stub fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#9ca3af,color:#374151,stroke-dasharray:5 3 subgraph STEP1["Step 1 — Base layer first"] B["Implement base layer
orchestration · HAL · routing"]:::base STUBS["Generate stubs
from G1 contracts"]:::stub TD["Top-down integration
base + all stubs"]:::test B --> STUBS --> TD end subgraph STEP2["Step 2 — Each module (DAG order)"] IMPL["Implement module
against contract"]:::mod UT["Unit test
in isolation"]:::test BU["Bottom-up integration
module + driver vs base"]:::test IMPL --> UT --> BU end TD --> STEP2 ``` Top-down (base → stubs) + bottom-up (module → driver → base) = **sandwich integration testing** [1][2][13]. ### Mandatory floor (VL-0) — cannot be skipped | Component | Always required | |---|---| | **Base layer** | Unit test + top-down integration with stubs | | **Each module** | Unit test + bottom-up integration with driver | --- ## 8 G2 — Adaptive Verification Gate ### 8.1 Verification levels ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef mandatory fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d,stroke-width:2px classDef optional fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f,stroke-dasharray:5 3 classDef hil fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-dasharray:5 3 VL0["VL-0 — Logic
Unit + sandwich integration
Deterministic vectors
MANDATORY"]:::mandatory VL1["VL-1 — Mock / SIL
+ mock-based system test
Synthetic I/Q · GnuRadio
OPTIONAL"]:::optional VL2["VL-2 — HIL
+ hardware-in-the-loop
Real HW · real RF
OPTIONAL"]:::hil VL0 -->|"user decides ▸"| VL1 -->|"user decides ▸"| VL2 ``` Each level includes all tests from the levels below. ### 8.2 Adaptive rule The user chooses the verification level per module, per cycle. Two constraints: 1. **Floor.** Every module reaches VL-0 in every cycle. 2. **Honesty.** No claim higher than what was tested. | Scenario | User declares | G2 checks | |---|---|---| | Fast iteration | VL-0 all | Unit + sandwich for every module | | DSP validation | VL-1 for DSP; VL-0 rest | Mock/SIL for DSP; unit for others | | Pre-release | VL-1 all; VL-2 for `iq_acquisition` | Mock all; HIL for acquisition | | Full release | All at `required_vl` | Every module at S1-declared max | ### 8.3 Sub-gates | Sub-gate | Fires when | Checks | |---|---|---| | **G2.0** | Always | Unit + sandwich integration pass | | **G2.1** | VL-1+ declared | Mock/SIL system tests pass; metrics within thresholds | | **G2.2** | VL-2 declared | HIL acceptance on real HW; measurements within criteria | --- ## 9 Feedback Routing V-SIL produces two types of feedback. They are structurally different and must not be conflated. ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef defect fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f classDef rfd fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d classDef stage fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,color:#0c4a6e classDef ext fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#6b7280,color:#1f2937,stroke-width:2px FAIL["Gate failure"]:::defect CLS{"Defect
or infeasibility?"} subgraph INTERNAL["Internal — Defect (fix within V-SIL)"] direction LR D_S1["S1 — design defect"]:::stage D_S2["S2 — module defect"]:::stage end subgraph EXTERNAL["External — RFD (Build Package must change)"] direction LR RFD["Request for Deviation"]:::rfd BP["Build Package
author"]:::ext RFD --> BP end FAIL --> CLS CLS -->|"implementation
or design"| INTERNAL CLS -->|"requirements
infeasible"| EXTERNAL ``` ### 9.1 Internal defect routing A **defect** means V-SIL can fix it internally. The implementation or the design is wrong, but the requirements are achievable. | Defect class | Routes to | Example | |---|---|---| | Design defect | S1 | DAG has undeclared dependency; interface contract incomplete | | Module defect | S2 | FFT module outputs wrong normalisation; classifier logic error | **Self-diagnosis:** if a module that was *not* changed fails during re-testing → undeclared dependency → design defect → S1. ### 9.2 Request for Deviation (RFD) An **RFD** means the Build Package requirements are **infeasible on the declared COTS platform**. V-SIL cannot fix it internally — the constraints themselves must change. V-SIL **suspends** until the Build Package is updated and re-enters at S0. An RFD can be emitted from **any stage**: | Discovered at | Example | |---|---| | S1 | Pipeline latency exceeds requirement under any partitioning on this HW | | G2.0 | Unit tests reveal that two normative requirements conflict mathematically | | G2.1 | SIL metrics show P_d and P_fa cannot simultaneously meet thresholds | | G2.2 | HIL shows real hardware noise floor exceeds assumed budget | ### 9.3 RFD contents Per ECSS [16], MIL-HDBK-61A [17], and NASA NPR 7150.2 [18]: ``` Request for Deviation — RFD-001 Conflicting requirements: STK-007: Latency ≤ 100 ms (source: ITU-R SM.1880) STK-012: P_d ≥ 0.95 @ 10 dB (source: national regulator) Evidence (from G2.1, VL-1): FFT 4096 → P_d 0.96, latency 142 ms — STK-012 met, STK-007 violated FFT 2048 → P_d 0.91, latency 71 ms — STK-007 met, STK-012 violated Trade-off options: A) Relax latency to ≤ 150 ms → both met B) Relax P_d to ≥ 0.92 → both met C) Dual-mode: fast (2048) + deep (4096) → both met, adds complexity Impact analysis: Option A: requires normative waiver from ITU-R SM.1880 §4.3 Option B: screening-grade only, not compliance-grade Option C: new module, new interface contract, S1 rework Recommendation: C ``` ### 9.4 Distinction summary ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef defect fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#78350f classDef rfd fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d D["Defect
Requirements achievable
Implementation wrong
Fix inside V-SIL"]:::defect R["RFD
Requirements infeasible
COTS cannot deliver both
Build Package must change"]:::rfd D ---|"different from"| R ``` --- ## 10 Terminal Output ``` Verified Prototype — V-SIL v3 Cycle: pre_release_01 Module evidence: iq_acquisition: VL-2 (HIL) — HackRF One, FM 88–108 MHz fft_engine: VL-1 (SIL) — GnuRadio mock, golden I/Q feature_extractor: VL-1 (SIL) — synthetic PSD at known SNR classifier: VL-0 (logic)— unit + sandwich integration audio_demod: VL-1 (SIL) — synthetic FM-modulated I/Q data_store: VL-0 (logic)— unit + sandwich integration Honesty declaration: VL-1 modules: VERIFIED against synthetic data. VL-2 modules: VALIDATED on real hardware. VL-0 modules: VERIFIED at logic level only. RFDs issued: 0 ``` --- ## 11 References [1] R. S. Pressman, B. R. Maxim, *Software Engineering*, 9th ed., 2020. [2] ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1:2022, "Software testing — Part 1." [3] Codeburst, "The Basics of Contract Tests," 2024. [4] L. Bass, P. Clements, R. [9] Sheridan Tech, "Design Validation vs Verification," Mar. 2026. [10] Augment Code, "Coordinator-Implementor-Verifier Pattern," Jun. 2026. [11] OPAL-RT, "Guide to HIL Testing," Sep. 2026.
